 Nairobi Among Counties to Experience Hot November as El Niño Starts - Kenya Met 
 -->
 --> 
 by Samuel Mwanawanjuguna on Sunday, 1 November 2026 - 1:12 pm 
 Kenyans crossing a road in Nairobi County during a rainy season in March 2023. 
 Photo 
 Nairobi News 
 -->
 Temperatures in Nairobi, Kiambu, and Murang'a will remain above average this November, despite forecasts of increased rainfall, according to the Kenya Meteorological Service Authority (KMSA). 
 According to the monthly forecast released on Friday, October 30, the mean temperatures around the country will remain elevated, with these counties ranging between 20°C and 30°C. 
 “The coolest conditions are generally expected over the highlands, where mean temperatures range between 15°C and 20°C, while the arid and semi-arid lowlands are likely to experience warmer conditions, with mean temperatures exceeding 28°C,” the Met said. 
 Nyandarua, Laikipia, Nyeri, Kirinyaga, Meru, Embu, and Tharaka-Nithi counties are the other counties expected to receive similar weather to Nairobi in November. 
 Motorists using a flooded highway during cold and rainy weather in Nairobi 
 KNA 
 During this period, Kenya Met forecasts minimum temperatures to range between 4°C and 20°C, meaning some nights will be hot while others are extremely cold. 
 Nakuru is also among the counties expected to experience warmer-than-average temperatures, with maximum temperatures ranging between 20°C and 30°C and minimum temperatures between 8°C and 20°C. 
 Kajiado, Machakos, and Mombasa are among a set of counties whose temperatures are set to rise as high as 35°C during this period. 
 The others are Kitui, Makueni, and Taita Taveta Counties, as well as the inland parts of Tana River County.  
 However, according to the met, Mombasa, Kilifi and Lamu will receive minimum temperatures of between 20°C and 25°C. 
 The forecast comes as Nairobi residents raise concerns about high temperatures, with the department projecting warmer-than-average conditions even as the October-December short rains season continues. 
 KMD explained that the southward migration of the Intertropical Convergence Zone across East Africa would contribute to relatively high temperatures, alongside increasing humidity and cloud cover associated with the rainfall season. 
 The department expects above-average rainfall in Nairobi, Kiambu and Nakuru, as well as dozens of other counties across the country. 
 It warned that increased rainfall could disrupt transport, particularly in urban areas where drainage systems may be overwhelmed, leading to traffic congestion and other transport challenges. 
 The department also cautioned that enhanced rainfall could increase the risk of flash floods, riverine flooding, landslides and damage to infrastructure in vulnerable areas.
